{{Infobox person|birth_date={{birth date|1505|6|26}}|death_date={{death date|1597|10|20}}|gender={{ill|Male (gender)|qid=Q6581097}}}}
'''Moriya Yorizane''' (守矢 頼真, {{ill|Eishō 2|ja|永正2年}} {{ill|May 25 (Lunisolar)|ja|5月25日 (旧暦)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/May 25 (lunar calendar)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q839582}} [{{ill|June 26, 1505|ja|1505th year 6月26日}}] – {{ill|Keichō 2|ja|慶長2年}} {{ill|September 10 (Lunisolar)|ja|9月10日 (旧暦)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/September 10 (lunar calendar)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q840113}} [{{ill|October 20, 1597|ja|1597th year 10月20日}}]) was a [[:en:Kannushi|Shinto priest]] during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|Sengoku period|qid=Q204023|lt=Sengoku period (Japan)}}. He served as the {{ill|jinchōkan|ja|神長官}} (chief priest) of {{ill|Suwa-taisha|abstract|Q218813|de|Suwa-Taisha|es|Suwa taisha|eu|Suwa taisha|fa|زیارتگاه بزرگ سووا|fr|Suwa-taisha|hu|Szuva templom|id|Kuil Suwa|it|Santuario di Suwa (Sohonsha)|ja|諏訪大社|ko|스와 대사|lt|Suvos maldykla|pl|Suwa Taisha|ru|Сува-тайся|simple|Suwa-taisha|tr|Suwa-taisha|zh|諏訪大社|qid=Q218813|lt=Suwa-taisha}} in the {{ill|Suwa District, Nagano|en|Suwa District, Nagano|qid=Q1131473|lt=Suwa District, Nagano}}, {{ill|Shinano Province|en|Shinano Province|qid=Q289250|lt=Shinano Province}}. According to the *{{ill|Suwa Shiryō Sōsho|ja|諏訪史料叢書}}*<ref>諏訪史料叢書 諏訪教育会著 1925-1952 12巻 守矢頼真書留(守矢頼真) 神長殿知行御検地[https://iss.ndl.go.jp/sp/show/R100000002-I000000871552-00/ 国会図書館]</ref>, he was the son of {{ill|Moriya Ariyoshi|ja|守矢有実}}. His son was {{ill|Moriya Nobuzane|ja|守矢信真}}. His initial name was Yorimitsu<ref>[https://kotobank.jp/word/%E5%AE%88%E7%9F%A2%E9%A0%BC%E5%AE%9F-1794824 コトバンク守矢頼実]参照。</ref>.

== Biography ==
The {{ill|Moriya clan|ja|守矢氏}} is believed to be descended from either {{ill|Moreya|en|Moreya|qid=Q11146526|lt=Moreya no Kami}} or {{ill|Mononobe no Moriya|en|Mononobe no Moriya|qid=Q2424736|lt=Mononobe no Moriya}}, but this remains uncertain. Yorizane served under the {{ill|Suwa clan|en|Suwa clan|qid=Q2975376|lt=Suwa clan}}, the {{ill|Hōri|ja|大祝|lt=Ōhori}} (chief priests) of Suwa Taisha, and frequently clashed with the {{ill|Negi|ja|禰宜|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Negi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11594490}} {{ill|Taifu|ja|太夫|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/tayū|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大夫|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大夫|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q14126428}} Yajima Mitsukiyo. He was initially at a disadvantage but regained his position during the appointment of {{ill|Suwa Yoritaka|ja|諏訪頼高|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Yoritaka|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11631969}} as Ōhori in {{ill|1538|ja|天文7年|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenbun 7|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 1538年|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 1538年|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q6470}} (1538). Yorizane also opposed {{ill|Suwa Yorishige (daimyo)|en|Suwa Yorishige (daimyo)|qid=Q2511179|lt=Suwa Yorishige (Sengoku period)}} regarding taxation on Suwa Taisha.

In {{ill|Tenbun 11|ja|天文11年}} (1542), when [[Takeda Shingen]]{{efn|Japanese feudal lord (1521–1573)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeda Shingen|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} of {{ill|Kai Province|en|Kai Province|qid=Q858076|lt=Kai Province}} initiated his invasion of Suwa, Yorishige was captured and later died. Yorizane supported the Takeda clan’s control of Suwa and earned their trust through rituals and prayers for victory (*{{ill|Moriya Yorishin|ja|守矢頼真書留|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moriya Yorizane Shokutō|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 守矢頼真|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 守矢頼真|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11450098}}*). In {{ill|Eiroku 2|ja|永禄2年}} (1559), he retired and passed the role of jinchōkan to his son Nobuzane. After the fall of the Takeda clan, Yorizane worked to revive the Suwa clan and contributed to the restoration of Suwa Taisha.

== *Moriya Yorizane Shokutō* ==
A personal record written by Yorizane, comprising one volume, documents the rituals and management of Suwa Taisha from his father’s era. The surviving entries span from {{ill|Tenbun 11|ja|天文11年}} (1542) to {{ill|Tenbun 21|ja|天文21年}} (1552). It includes key historical events, such as the birth of Yorishige’s heir in April 1542 and Yorishige’s death in July. While it initially covers the Takeda invasion of Suwa, later entries focus on shrine administration. The original manuscript was preserved by the Moriya family, and its text has been reproduced in collections such as the *{{ill|Q85876578|ja|信濃史料叢書|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano Shiryō Sōsho|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q85876578}}* and the *{{ill|Yamanashi Prefectural History|ja|山梨県史}}*.

== *Shinshi Ontō no Nikki* ==
A record of the shrine's annual rituals and notable events from {{ill|Kyōroku 1|ja|享禄元年}} (1528) to {{ill|Tenbun 23|ja|天文23年}} (1554). It describes significant occurrences, such as the peace negotiations between Takeda Nobutora and Suwa Hekiunsai at the Sakai River in 1535, and events leading to Takeda Shingen's invasion of Suwa. While the original manuscript has not been located, a copy made in {{ill|Bunka 14|ja|文化14年}} (1817) has been used for reproductions in historical collections.
